title: diggs-diff 1.0
description: The difference between two DIGGS files at model level, as pydiggs.diff.compare() writes it (pyDIGGS 1.12 and later). Open for consumers: objects accept unknown fields, so a 1.0 consumer accepts any 1.x document. A new optional field is a minor version; anything else is a new major. Nothing is converted: a change of unit is a change.

$schema.description: URL of the schema the document follows.

identical.description: True only when nothing differs and the comparison finished (complete).

complete.description: False when a limit stopped the comparison or a file was read in part; see limits_hit and notes.

limits_hit.description: What stopped the comparison; empty when complete.

summary.description: Node counts per collection (features, samples, measurements, layers, components ...). Exact when only max_changes stopped the list; partial after a time_budget stop.

value_changes.description: How many values differ (every listed value change counts, listed or not).

reformatted.description: How many values are written differently but are equal (1.50 and 1.5).

changes.description: Ordered by collection, then key, then path. At most max_changes entries (changes plus value changes).

notes.description: Findings of step diff: diff.ambiguous-match, diff.limit, diff.timeout.

truncated.description: True when name or a key was cut to 200 characters.

path.description: Which value: name, params.<element>, interval.top, results[0].columns[<key>].cells[@<index>] ...

old.description: The value in the old file as JSON (a quantity is its text and unit, e.g. "1.50 ft"); null when the old file has none. Text is cut to 200 characters and lists to 200 items.

new.description: The value in the new file; null when the new file has none.

at.description: XPath of the node in the new file (the old file for a removed node).

truncated.description: True when old or new was cut.
